content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":4,"description_fidelity":4,"readability_1x":5,"pixel_craft":4,"palette_discipline":8,"appeal":5},"score":48,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The large rectangular white eye panel makes the body read more like a helmet or ghost than a floating squid.","The lower cyan mass forms one blunt block instead of distinct tentacles gathered for a swimming thrust.","The right-side appendage is visually detached and resembles an arm or tail rather than part of a radial tentacle arrangement.","The bottom and right contours use heavy, square black masses inconsistent with Mega Man 2-3's economical 1-pixel outlining.","Several staircase transitions around the dome, eye panel, and lower body are lumpy rather than deliberately clustered.","Both eyes are featureless black slots; the described red warning flash is not represented in the shown state.","At 1x, the eye panel remains visible, but the propulsion anatomy and mine-like function are unclear.","The palette is suitably limited, but the broad white area dominates and leaves little room for Capcom-style cyan volume accents."],"fixes":["Reduce the white eye panel by one pixel around its perimeter and separate the eyes with a cleaner central bridge.","Round the dome with deliberate 2-1 or 2-2 pixel stair steps and keep the exterior outline predominantly one pixel thick.","Split the lower cyan block into three short tentacle tips with one-pixel black gaps; angle the outer tips inward for the gathered pose.","Attach the right-side form directly to the body or replace it with a symmetric side tentacle so it does not appear to float separately.","Remove the solid black bottom-right blocks and restore cyan interior pixels bounded by a clean one-pixel contour.","Give each eye a compact pupil cluster and create an alternate warning frame that swaps the eye interiors to a single NES red.","Add one small cyan highlight cluster near the upper-left dome while keeping each tile within the existing limited palette.","Design a second thrust frame with the tentacles extended downward or backward to make the pulsing swim action readable."]}
